title: Two hook tableaux of size 12 with equal multisets of 8-minors: the k+4 reconstruction conjecture fails
exact_endpoint: TabMinors.not_conjecture : ¬ TabMinors.Conjecture, where Conjecture := ∀ k n, 1 ≤ k → k + 4 ≤ n → ∀ T U, IsSYT n T → IsSYT n U → minors k T = minors k U → T = U
scope: Erickson-Herden-Meddaugh-Sepanski-Hammon-Mohn-Ruiz-Bolanos (arXiv:2307.13161; J. Combin. Theory Ser. A 209 (2025) 105950), Conjecture conj:k+4: for n >= k+4 the multiset mM_k(T) of k-minors (over all jeu de taquin deletion sequences) determines a standard Young tableau. False at k = 8, n = 12. The hooks T1 (first row 1 5 7 8 12) and T2 (first row 1 2 3 7 10 11) are distinct and have identical mM_8 (19,958,400 minors each). Supplementary (ordinary mathematics, not Lean): a hook weight formula shows that no bound n >= k + c works for any constant c, with an explicit n = k+5 failure at k = 11.
source_targets: W. Q. Erickson et al., arXiv:2307.13161 Conjecture conj:k+4; JCTA 209 (2025) 105950
root_fix: annotation-only: noncomputable added to slide, del, minors, den, ins, norm and step, removing compiler-generated partial companions (tabminors-parent-check-r1)
substantive_reason: It refutes a published (JCTA 2025) reconstruction conjecture, still presented as open in February 2025, at its smallest case. The failure is structural (no constant c works), it is not an endpoint or convention artefact, and it was not visible from the source's computations (k <= 5).
